cls: Leukocyte (granulocyte colony-stimulating) growth factor - long-acting G-CSF
pharm: Pegylated, long-acting recombinant human granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) that stimulates neutrophil production to reduce chemotherapy-induced febrile neutropenia.
quick: 6 mg subcutaneously once per chemotherapy cycle
Subcutaneous injection; not affected by food
Limited data; use only if clearly needed
Compatible; minimal expected transfer (large protein, likely degraded in GI tract)
CBC/platelets, splenic enlargement, respiratory and allergic reactions
summary: Pegfilgrastim is a long-acting, pegylated recombinant human G-CSF used to decrease the incidence of infection (febrile neutropenia) in patients with non-myeloid malignancies receiving myelosuppressive chemotherapy, and to increase survival in patients acutely exposed to myelosuppressive radiation (Hematopoietic Subsyndrome of Acute Radiation Syndrome). The usual adult dose is a single 6 mg subcutaneous injection once per chemotherapy cycle, and it must NOT be given between 14 days before and 24 hours after cytotoxic chemotherapy. Key risks include fatal splenic rupture, acute respiratory distress syndrome, serious allergic reactions, and sickle cell crises.
indications: Decrease the incidence of infection, as manifested by febrile neutropenia, in patients with non-myeloid malignancies receiving myelosuppressive anti-cancer drugs associated with a clinically significant incidence of febrile neutropenia
Increase survival in patients acutely exposed to myelosuppressive doses of radiation (Hematopoietic Subsyndrome of Acute Radiation Syndrome)

dosage.d: 6 mg as a single subcutaneous injection once per chemotherapy cycle
dosage.n: Do NOT administer between 14 days before and 24 hours after cytotoxic chemotherapy

dosage.c: Hematopoietic Subsyndrome of Acute Radiation Syndrome
dosage.d: Two 6 mg doses one week apart; first dose as soon as possible after suspected/confirmed exposure
dosage.n: Estimate absorbed radiation dose; treat promptly
Do not use single fixed 6 mg dose in small children

admin: Give as a single subcutaneous injection (abdomen, thigh, or upper arm); rotate sites
Do NOT administer between 14 days before and 24 hours after cytotoxic chemotherapy
Allow prefilled syringe/on-body injector to reach room temperature; do not shake; inspect for particulates
Use weight-based dosing for pediatric patients weighing less than 45 kg
For the on-body injector, instruct patients to report suspected device failure (risk of missed/incomplete dose)
moa: Pegfilgrastim is a colony-stimulating factor produced by covalent conjugation of recombinant human G-CSF (filgrastim) to polyethylene glycol, which prolongs its half-life. It binds to specific G-CSF receptors on hematopoietic cells, stimulating the proliferation, differentiation, commitment, and functional activation of neutrophil progenitor cells. This increases circulating neutrophil counts, reducing the duration of severe neutropenia and the incidence of febrile neutropenia after myelosuppressive chemotherapy.

absolute: History of serious allergic reactions to pegfilgrastim products or filgrastim products (including anaphylaxis)
relative: Sickle cell disease/trait (risk of severe, sometimes fatal, sickle cell crisis)
Concurrent use with the 14-day-before / 24-hour-after chemotherapy window
Known sensitivity to acrylic adhesives (on-body injector)
monitor: Allergic reactions and sickle cell crisis

preg: Available data are limited; pegfilgrastim is a large pegylated protein with limited placental transfer expected. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: There are no data on presence in human milk; G-CSF is a large glycoprotein likely degraded in the infant GI tract, so systemic absorption is not expected. Breastfeeding is generally considered compatible.
renal: No dosage adjustment is necessary in patients with renal impairment.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is necessary in patients with hepatic impairment.

major: Cytotoxic chemotherapy - do not administer within the 14 days before to 24 hours after window due to sensitivity of rapidly dividing myeloid cells
moderate: Lithium - may potentiate the release of neutrophils; monitor neutrophil counts
Drugs that may increase MDS/AML risk in breast/lung cancer when combined with chemo/radiotherapy
minor: No significant pharmacokinetic drug interactions established
interactions.diagnostics: Can cause transiently positive bone-imaging changes due to increased hematopoietic activity; transiently elevated alkaline phosphatase, LDH, and uric acid may occur.

serious: Sickle cell crisis (can be fatal) in patients with sickle cell disease/trait
rare: Myelodysplastic syndrome / acute myeloid leukemia (in breast/lung cancer with chemo/radiotherapy)
emergency: Splenic rupture (left upper abdominal or shoulder-tip pain)

monitoring: Complete blood count and platelet counts periodically
Left upper quadrant or shoulder-tip pain (splenic enlargement/rupture)
Signs of allergic reaction and, in sickle cell patients, sickle crisis
Renal function (glomerulonephritis), and MDS/AML signs in breast/lung cancer patients
counsel: This is given as one injection per chemotherapy cycle, not on the same day as your chemo drugs
Bone or muscle pain is common; ask your team about appropriate pain relief
Seek urgent care for upper-left belly or shoulder pain, trouble breathing, or signs of allergic reaction
If using an on-body injector, watch it deliver fully and call your provider if you suspect it failed
Tell your team if you have sickle cell disease or any allergy to G-CSF products or acrylic adhesives
pk: Neutrophil count rises within the first days after a dose
Serum concentration peaks roughly 1-3 days after subcutaneous injection
Refrigerate at 2-8 C (36-46 F); do not freeze or shake; protect from light
pearls: Long-acting pegylated G-CSF - one 6 mg dose per chemo cycle replaces daily filgrastim injections
NEVER give between 14 days before and 24 hours after cytotoxic chemotherapy
Watch for fatal splenic rupture (left upper quadrant/shoulder pain) and ARDS
Discontinue permanently for serious allergic reactions; discontinue if sickle cell crisis occurs
Not indicated for peripheral blood progenitor cell mobilization for stem cell transplant
missed: Pegfilgrastim is dosed once per chemotherapy cycle rather than daily; if a planned dose is missed or delayed, contact the oncology team to reschedule while respecting the requirement not to dose within 24 hours after chemotherapy.
overdose: There is limited experience with overdose. Higher-than-recommended doses may produce leukocytosis and bone pain. Management is supportive; monitor complete blood counts. Discontinue and treat symptomatically if leukocytosis or adverse effects occur.
